title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 15
statement: Right triangles \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) have areas \(1\) and \(2\), respectively. A side of \(T_1\) is congruent to a side of \(T_2,\) and a different side of \(T_1\) is congruent to a different side of \(T_2.\) What is the square of the product of the lengths of the other (third) sides of \(T_1\) and \(T_2?\)

solutions.text:
Let the two shared side lengths be \(a\le b\). Because the triangles have different areas, the shared sides cannot play the same roles in both triangles. Thus the area-\(2\) triangle has legs \(a\) and \(b\), while the area-\(1\) triangle has leg \(a\), other leg \(\sqrt{b^2-a^2}\), and hypotenuse \(b\).

The product of the two non-shared third sides is \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\sqrt{b^2-a^2}\), whose square is \(b^4-a^4\).

Using the areas, \(\dfrac{ab}{2}=2\) and \(\dfrac{a\sqrt{b^2-a^2}}{2}=1\). Hence \(a^2b^2=16\) and \(a^2(b^2-a^2)=4\), so \(a^4=12\). Then \(b^4=\dfrac{256}{12}=\dfrac{64}{3}\), and \(b^4-a^4=\dfrac{28}{3}\). Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Let the two shared side lengths be \(a\le b\)
Use the two area equations to find \(b^4-a^4\)
